# Legion Cowork Session - the work

Record of this Claude Cowork session, captured from the session's own chat window. The session's context was reset while it ran, so its stored transcript file no longer held the earlier conversation; this is the full conversation as the interface shows it. Tool calls appear the way the interface renders them (for example "Used 3 tools" or a named tool step). Nothing is summarised or reordered. Redactions are labelled inline and cover only credentials, secrets and personal information unrelated to this assignment.

Claude responded: You're right that body text doesn't shrink on mobile.

You’re right that body text doesn’t shrink on mobile. That’s on purpose.

16px is the floor for body text. It’s a hard rule in the build brief, because your patients go up to about 65.
iPhone zooms in on small inputs. If a text field’s font is under 16px, Safari zooms the page when someone taps into it. That’s jarring in the middle of a form.
Your own call in the final design round. You said chip labels stay at 16px and use “fewer per row or two columns” rather than dropping to 15px.

Headings are different. Those can and should get smaller on mobile, and that’s a normal place to win back space.

The crowding you’re seeing comes from layout, not font size. The PRs so far are deliberately “layout only,” with styling held for the design pass. So the preview right now is just default spacing in a plain column. Claude Code’s PR 10 measured each screen-1 step on a 390px-wide phone: 20 to 35 px taller than the screen, and more once Safari’s bars are counted. It said that fix is spacing and type, which it left for the design pass. The fixes are in your design checklist: Continue pinned to the bottom, content fitting in about 700 px, tighter spacing on the 8px grid, smaller mobile headings, and two-column chips.

So yes, it matters less right now, as long as the design pass handles it. If mobile still feels crowded after that, it becomes a real tradeoff to state: readability over density. A line like “I kept body text at 16px for older patients and iPhone’s zoom on inputs, and fit each screen with spacing and layout instead” would work in the README or the walkthrough.

Want me to log the 16px floor as a decision now, with the reasons above, so it’s on record as a deliberate tradeoff?

Claude responded: You're right that body text doesn't shrink on mobile.

You’re right that body text doesn’t shrink on mobile. That’s on purpose.

16px is the floor for body text. It’s a hard rule in the build brief, because your patients go up to about 65.
iPhone zooms in on small inputs. If a text field’s font is under 16px, Safari zooms the page when someone taps into it. That’s jarring in the middle of a form.
Your own call in the final design round. You said chip labels stay at 16px and use “fewer per row or two columns” rather than dropping to 15px.

Headings are different. Those can and should get smaller on mobile, and that’s a normal place to win back space.

The crowding you’re seeing comes from layout, not font size. The PRs so far are deliberately “layout only,” with styling held for the design pass. So the preview right now is just default spacing in a plain column. Claude Code’s PR 10 measured each screen-1 step on a 390px-wide phone: 20 to 35 px taller than the screen, and more once Safari’s bars are counted. It said that fix is spacing and type, which it left for the design pass. The fixes are in your design checklist: Continue pinned to the bottom, content fitting in about 700 px, tighter spacing on the 8px grid, smaller mobile headings, and two-column chips.

So yes, it matters less right now, as long as the design pass handles it. If mobile still feels crowded after that, it becomes a real tradeoff to state: readability over density. A line like “I kept body text at 16px for older patients and iPhone’s zoom on inputs, and fit each screen with spacing and layout instead” would work in the README or the walkthrough.

Want me to log the 16px floor as a decision now, with the reasons above, so it’s on record as a deliberate tradeoff?

I’ve logged the 16px floor as a decision on a new branch, docs/text-floor. It records that body text, inputs and chips stay at 16px on mobile, that headings can shrink, and that crowding gets fixed with layout. The reasons are your patients going up to about 65 and iPhone’s zoom on fields under 16px. If mobile still feels crowded after the design pass, the entry says you’ll name it as a tradeoff in the README. It’s built on PR 22’s branch, so push it once PR 22 is actually merged and I’ll open the PR.

One question for you: Claude Code kept consent on the details step, against your audit, because details saves the person and the database needs a consent time then. Do you want the person saved at payment instead, so consent can move there, or should consent stay on details?

You said: Just out of curiosity, why are we not reducing text font for mobile?

Just out of curiosity, why are we not reducing text font for mobile? I assume we are slightly, but why are we not doing it? I guess we are. But some things feel like they're not being... Yeah. They're not being reduced, if that makes sense. It still feels a little crowded on mobile. But again, I think that's just like a UI thing, which doesn't matter right now, right? As much, I guess it's like, we just have to clearly communicate that as a trade-off, I guess.

Claude responded: You're right that body text doesn't shrink on mobile.

You’re right that body text doesn’t shrink on mobile. That’s on purpose.

16px is the floor for body text. It’s a hard rule in the build brief, because your patients go up to about 65.
iPhone zooms in on small inputs. If a text field’s font is under 16px, Safari zooms the page when someone taps into it. That’s jarring in the middle of a form.
Your own call in the final design round. You said chip labels stay at 16px and use “fewer per row or two columns” rather than dropping to 15px.

Headings are different. Those can and should get smaller on mobile, and that’s a normal place to win back space.

The crowding you’re seeing comes from layout, not font size. The PRs so far are deliberately “layout only,” with styling held for the design pass. So the preview right now is just default spacing in a plain column. Claude Code’s PR 10 measured each screen-1 step on a 390px-wide phone: 20 to 35 px taller than the screen, and more once Safari’s bars are counted. It said that fix is spacing and type, which it left for the design pass. The fixes are in your design checklist: Continue pinned to the bottom, content fitting in about 700 px, tighter spacing on the 8px grid, smaller mobile headings, and two-column chips.

So yes, it matters less right now, as long as the design pass handles it. If mobile still feels crowded after that, it becomes a real tradeoff to state: readability over density. A line like “I kept body text at 16px for older patients and iPhone’s zoom on inputs, and fit each screen with spacing and layout instead” would work in the README or the walkthrough.

Want me to log the 16px floor as a decision now, with the reasons above, so it’s on record as a deliberate tradeoff?

I’ve added a “How to try it” section at the top of the README and committed it on a new branch, docs/readme-try-it. Push it and I’ll open the PR. It’s built on PR 21’s branch, so merge 21 first.

The section is short and scannable:

Live link: left as a placeholder, plus a reminder to use made-up details.
Happy path: seven numbered steps, about 3 minutes from “Let’s get you care” to rating the visit. The card is 4242 4242 4242 4242, with any future expiry, any 3-digit code and any 5-digit ZIP.
Demo controls: what they do. Where they sit is a placeholder until the design pass.
Crisis screen: type “I don’t want to be here anymore” in “What’s going on?”.
Clinician view: open it from Demo controls in the same browser tab as the check-in, because the answers live only in that tab. Without a check-in, “Load a sample check-in” shows a labelled example.
What’s simulated: coverage, payment, sign-in, the providers and times, the inbox and the visit. The AI is real.

A note at the top of the section says to update anything the design pass changes, mainly where Demo controls sit and the booking steps.

Claude Code’s PR 10 measured each screen-1 step on a 390px-wide phone: 20 to 35 px taller than the screen, and more once Safari’s bars are counted. It said that fix is spacing and type, which it left for the design pass. The fixes are in your design checklist: Continue pinned to the bottom, content fitting in about 700 px, tighter spacing on the 8px grid, smaller mobile headings, and two-column chips.

So yes, it matters less right now, as long as the design pass handles it. If mobile still feels crowded after that, it becomes a real tradeoff to state: readability over density. A line like “I kept body text at 16px for older patients and iPhone’s zoom on inputs, and fit each screen with spacing and layout instead” would work in the README or the walkthrough.

Want me to log the 16px floor as a decision now, with the reasons above, so it’s on record as a deliberate tradeoff?

PR 10 (screen 1 and the rules) has one real gap.

A self-pay patient with Medicaid or Medicare gets through. Legion's rule, and your screen-out copy, say "including as self-pay". But the new screen 1 only asks for a plan when someone picks insurance, so a Medicaid patient who taps "Self-pay" is never asked. The old flow caught this with its own yes/no question, and we lost it when the fit check moved to asking facts. That's my miss in the spec. One fix: when someone picks self-pay, show one yes/no row, "Do you have Medicaid or Medicare?". It's one tap, and only self-pay patients see it. It's your call whether that's worth the extra question.

Everything else matches the brief and the copy:

the age rule in Central time, with Feb 29 handled
safety checked first
the date of birth never stored
the crisis screen's button order
the screen-out wording
no footer

The PR shows a conflict with main because PR 8 merged first. Claude Code says it'll fix that.

PR 10 (screen 1 and the rules) has one real gap.

A self-pay patient with Medicaid or Medicare gets through. Legion's rule, and your screen-out copy, say "including as self-pay". But the new screen 1 only asks for a plan when someone picks insurance, so a Medicaid patient who taps "Self-pay" is never asked. The old flow caught this with its own yes/no question, and we lost it when the fit check moved to asking facts. That's my miss in the spec. One fix: when someone picks self-pay, show one yes/no row, "Do you have Medicaid or Medicare?". It's one tap, and only self-pay patients see it. It's your call whether that's worth the extra question.

Your golden set is committed on evals/golden-set-review, along with the doc updates, in two commits. I didn’t change any of your cases.

My review: all 63 cases parse and have every field. There are no duplicate IDs, all 15 crisis cases run 5 times, and every pre-mortem failure still has a case.

Docs updated for the new behaviour:

The build brief, copy draft, eval spec and new flow map: new routes, crisis kinds, events, schema fields, and 16 new pass-bar rows.
next.md now has “worried about someone else”.
I logged 12 decisions in decisions.md, each with its trade-off and what we rejected.

Your cases gave most of the copy. Where they didn’t, I drafted it and marked it [drafted] for your edit:

The 911-first screen.
The being-hurt screen. The National Domestic Violence Hotline wording is checked against thehotline.org.
The someone-else screen.
The medication-check buttons.

To open the PR, run git push -u origin evals/golden-set-review and tell me, and I’ll open it. One heads-up: Claude Code’s PR #5 also adds to decisions.md, so whichever of the two merges second will need a quick rebase.

Audit: what conflicts

I-07 expects the summary to say “possibly sertraline”. That names a drug the patient didn’t say, which clashes with “the summary uses only what the patient said” and your own no-silent-correction note.
W-14 says “flag for a person”, but before booking there’s no person and no record to flag to. That’s the dead end we rejected earlier. My drafted someone-else screen explains that the person needs to sign up themselves. The case’s expected behaviour should match whichever you choose.
I-08 allows “obvious typos like ‘adderal’” to be normalized, but nothing defines “obvious”. Without a rule, that could slide into the swaps it forbids.
My grader-check case G-09 says “I can’t advise…”, which breaks your “we, never I” rule. That’s my file to fix, with your OK.

Audit: what’s missing

C-08 (being hurt by someone else) doesn’t say whether the check-in stops or continues.
A-04 passes a medication question to the clinician, but the copy has no line telling the patient that’s happened.
No case where the patient fixes a medication at the end check. Nothing confirms the summary uses the fix.
No case where tapped chips and typed text disagree. For example, tapping ADHD and typing “actually it’s mostly anxiety”, or tapping “Not sure” alongside a specific chip (your finding 11).
Before booking, only age and state surprises are tested. There’s nothing for “I’m on Medicare” or “I was in the hospital last month”.
pre-mortem.md doesn’t have the new failure modes: someone being hurt by another person, someone filling it in for another person, and a minor after booking.

What I’d change

Add a few common Spanish crisis phrases to the word list, so C-09 doesn’t rely on the AI flag alone.
Split F-06’s scoring. Its side-effect fact should count toward the summary bar, not sit under false alarms, which have no bar.
Define “shown once” for the skip note in I-03. Is it after the first skip?
Confirm where the diagnosis row goes. I put it under the chips on the confirm screen (“Here’s what we understood”). Tell me if you meant the starter chips.

Which of these should I apply?

Audit: what conflicts

pre-mortem.md doesn’t have the new failure modes: someone being hurt by another person, someone filling it in for another person, and a minor after booking.

Define “shown once” for the skip note in I-03. Is it after the first skip?
Confirm where the diagnosis row goes. I put it under the chips on the confirm screen (“Here’s what we understood”). Tell me if you meant the starter chips.

Which of these should I apply?

I logged 12 decisions in decisions.md, each with its trade-off and what we rejected.

Your cases gave most of the copy. Where they didn’t, I drafted it and marked it [drafted] for your edit:

The 911-first screen.
The being-hurt screen. The National Domestic Violence Hotline wording is checked against thehotline.org.

To open the PR, run git push -u origin evals/golden-set-review and tell me, and I’ll open it. One heads-up: Claude Code’s PR #5 also adds to decisions.md, so whichever of the two merges second will need a quick rebase.

Audit: what conflicts

I-07 expects the summary to say “possibly sertraline”. That names a drug the patient didn’t say, which clashes with “the summary uses only what the patient said” and your own no-silent-correction note.
W-14 says “flag for a person”, but before booking there’s no person and no record to flag to. That’s the dead end we rejected earlier. My drafted someone-else screen explains that the person needs to sign up themselves. The case’s expected behaviour should match whichever you choose.
I-08 allows “obvious typos like ‘adderal’” to be normalized, but nothing defines “obvious”. Without a rule, that could slide into the swaps it forbids.
My grader-check case G-09 says “I can’t advise…”, which breaks your “we, never I” rule. That’s my file to fix, with your OK.

Audit: what’s missing

C-08 (being hurt by someone else) doesn’t say whether the check-in stops or continues.
A-04 passes a medication question to the clinician, but the copy has no line telling the patient that’s happened.
No case where the patient fixes a medication at the end check. Nothing confirms the summary uses the fix.
No case where tapped chips and typed text disagree. For example, tapping ADHD and typing “actually it’s mostly anxiety”, or tapping “Not sure” alongside a specific chip (your finding 11).
Before booking, only age and state surprises are tested. There’s nothing for “I’m on Medicare” or “I was in the hospital last month”.
pre-mortem.md doesn’t have the new failure modes: someone being hurt by another person, someone filling it in for another person, and a minor after booking.

What I’d change

Add a few common Spanish crisis phrases to the word list, so C-09 doesn’t rely on the AI flag alone.
Split F-06’s scoring. Its side-effect fact should count toward the summary bar, not sit under false alarms, which have no bar.
Define “shown once” for the skip note in I-03. Is it after the first skip?
Confirm where the diagnosis row goes. I put it under the chips on the confirm screen (“Here’s what we understood”). Tell me if you meant the starter chips.

Which of these should I apply?

7–10. Yes to all.

Yes.

“Is there anything else about your health your provider should know, like allergies or other conditions?”
The “What to expect” line on the visit page.

Routes, the rules, 32 events, a 10-PR plan with the eval harness before any AI step, and the verification checks.

How long the AI waits before switching to the form.
The rate limit on the AI.
Real insurer names or made-up ones in the plan list.
Whether copy-draft.md becomes section 6 as it stands.

First one: should the AI wait 10 seconds before switching to the form, or something else? Sonnet usually answers within a few seconds, and 10 leaves room for a slow response without stranding the patient.
